JUDGMENT

This is a charge sheet filed by the P.S.I of Konanakunte P.S. against the accused No.1 & 2 for the offences punishable U/sec. 63 of Copy Right Act and 420 R/w 34 of IPC.
02.

The brief facts of the prosecution case is that, on 18.09.2018 at about 4.15 hours, within the limits of Konanakunte Police Station, situated at Gajananda Automobiles shop No.1 and Surabhi Automobiles No.90/90 shop No.2, SP Complex, Kembhathhalli Main Road, Gottigere, Bannerghatta Road, Bengaluru. CW.1 got information that, the accused No.1 & 2 selling C.C.No.789/2020 of spurious/counterfeit spare parts of TVS Motors Limited of CW.1 without obtaining any permission from company authority and selling duplicate TVS Motors spare parts to the public at large and thus the accused persons have committed the offences punishable U/sec. 63 of Copy Right Act and 420 R/w 34 of IPC.
03.
After filing of charge sheet, this court took cognizance for the offences punishable U/sec. 63 of Copy Right Act and 420 R/w 34 of IPC and issued summons to the accused persons.
Accordingly the accused persons appeared before the court through their counsel.

Later on, charge sheet copies and prosecution papers were furnished to the accused persons under Sec.207 of Cr.P.C.
04.
Heard both side on framing of charge, perused the prosecution papers.
As there are sufficient materials to frame the charge against the accused persons, the charges has been framed and the same were read over to them, but they pleaded not guilty and claimed for trial.
Hence the case was posted for prosecution evidence.

The prosecution in order to prove its case has not examined any of the witnesses, in spite of repeated issuance of NBW and proclamation against CW.1 to 7 the concerned agency failed to execute the same to the said witnesses and bring them before this court, hence prayer of learned Sr.APP is rejected.
CW.1 to 7 were dropped and closed the side of the prosecution evidence, as there is no incriminating circumstances against the accused persons.

Hence, the accused statement U/Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. is dispensed with and posted for judgment.
06.
In order to prove the guilt of the offence as alleged against the accused persons by the prosecution, the prosecution has not at all examined any one of the witnesses.
It is relevant to note that, the prosecution has cited 7 witnesses.
In spite of issuance of summons warrant against the CW.1 to 7 the prosecution has utterly failed to secure the presence of CW.1 to 7.

Though this Court Harish Kumar K vs Sharavan Praja Path on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157762530/
2 issued coercive process of witness warrant against CW.1 to 7, they have not appeared before the court.

sentences.text: Therefore, this Court dropped out CW.1 to 7.
Therefore, this Court proceed in accordance with law.
Hence, C.C.No.789/2020 prosecution has utterly failed to prove the guilt of the offence as alleged against the accused persons beyond reasonable doubt.
Thereby accused are entitled for the benefit of doubt.

Hence, I proceed to pass following;
ORDER
By exercising powers conferred U/sec.248(1) of Cr.P.C., the accused No.1 & 2 are acquitted for the offences punishable U/sec.63 of Copy Right Act and 420 R/w 34 of IPC.

The bail bond and surety bond of the accused No.1 & 2 shall continue in force for a period of 6 months for the purposes of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C.
The accused No.1 & 2 are set at liberty.
The Sl.No.1 & 2 properties reported in PF No.199/2018 are ordered to be destroyed as worthless after appeal period is over.

Further, the properties mentioned in Sl.No.3 & 4 are being the cash of Rs.1,200/-
& Rs.3,000/- respectively confiscated to state.
(Dictated Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected and then pronounced by me in the open court this 5th day of June 2025).
2025 (Sri Vinod Balnaik) IX Addl.
Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru City.
